system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) at work
G2: production on-call
G3: cluster administration
G4: CKA certification (not yet passed)
G5: Terraform at work

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing CKA or Terraform Associate as held certifications
T2: Claiming AWS/GCP production experience or 'managed Kubernetes clusters'
T3: Presenting homelab tools (Argo CD, Prometheus, Terraform) as work experience
T4: Claiming production on-call / SRE incident ownership
T5: Retitling her current job as 'DevOps Engineer' instead of her real title
T6: Old cover letter is addressed to her current employer and says she is at Brightmill

# OUTPUT 1: CV
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer transitioning toward DevOps and platform engineering, with 7 years of experience
including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD and test infrastructure. Owns merge-request ephemeral
environments used by three product teams. Experienced with Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes
deployments, with personal hands-on practice in k3s, GitOps and Terraform. Brings an analytical approach to
improving pipeline performance and reliability. Owned GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and wrote the
internal CI guide used in onboarding.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform (personal projects),
Kubernetes (namespace-level access; basic), k3s, Argo CD
Monitoring & Data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Languages & Scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems & Tools: Linux, Git, Ansible (basic)
Cloud & Infrastructure Projects: AWS EC2 and S3 fundamentals (personal free-tier use); Hetzner VPS
(personal project); Terraform (personal projects)
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw 2021–Present
• Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), coordinating build, unit, integration and
end-to-end test stages, artifact publishing, and pipeline improvements across the teams.
• Profiled and improved CI pipelines across three teams.
• Own merge-request ephemeral environments used by three product teams.
• Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of about 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to
below 1%.
• Owned CI test-result reporting and flaky-test visibility for three product teams.
• Write Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
• Wrote the internal guide to how CI works, used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.
QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw 2019–2021
• Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
• Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
• Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.
Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House 2018–2019
• Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.
SELECTED PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal 2024–2025
• Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository
using Argo CD.
• Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS certificate
management.
• Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform as a personal project; used Ansible at a
basic level.
Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health 2023–2024
• Delivered short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments with seeded data, deployed via Helm to a
shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
• Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against each
environment.
• Automated environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health 2022
• Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and split end-to-end
tests into a separate stage.
• Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health 2023
• Collected CI test results using Python and the GitLab API, stored results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana
dashboards for flaky tests by team.
• Helped teams identify top offenders as the flaky test rate fell from 7% to below 1%.
EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology 2018
CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation — exam scheduled for January 2027; not yet certified.
LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. In my current role at
Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines and merge-request environments used by
three product teams, supporting the delivery and testing of services through reliable, repeatable
infrastructure workflows. I’m looking to build on this experience in a platform and
infrastructure engineering role, and Corvale’s work connecting a new train fleet with cloud
services makes this opportunity particularly compelling.
I’ve improved CI pipelines across three teams, reducing average run time from 38 to 14 minutes
and monthly runner costs by about 30%. I designed and delivered short-lived application and
PostgreSQL environments for each merge request, with seeded data, Helm-based deployment to
a shared Kubernetes cluster, end-to-end test execution and automatic cleanup after merge or 48
hours of inactivity. These projects required profiling systems, proposing and coordinating
changes across three product teams, and bringing developers and QA stakeholders along
through clearer CI documentation and visibility into flaky tests. I wrote Odrava’s internal guide
to how CI works, which is used in onboarding, and mentored two QA interns.
My hands-on infrastructure engineering experience includes Linux, GitLab CI, Docker,
Helm-based Kubernetes deployments, namespace-level operation of shared environments, and
infrastructure-as-code practice with Terraform. Outside work, I built a three-node k3s homelab
with GitOps deployments, monitoring, ingress and TLS certificate management, and provisioned
a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform. I have also used AWS EC2 and S3 at a fundamentals
level through personal free-tier projects. This has given me a practical foundation in
infrastructure-as-code, automation, observability and test infrastructure, while my Terraform
experience to date has been through personal projects.
Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on teams owning systems and solving
problems collaboratively resonate with how I’ve approached improving shared CI and test
environments. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could support the
Fleet Connectivity team as it shapes reliable, observable infrastructure for the new fleet.
Thank you for your consideration.
Marta Kowal-Brandt

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
